c.tagline: Argentina's high-altitude wine capital at the foot of the Andes.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis and remises are metered and cheap; radio taxis and apps (Uber, Cabify, DiDi) are widely used and often cheaper for airport runs.

emergency.note: Dial 911 for police and general emergencies; 107 is the ambulance/medical line and 100 is the fire brigade.

hood_landmark.Chacras de Coria: Chacras de Coria plaza, Luján de Cuyo

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Plaza Independencia and the bus terminal; caution in Parque San Martín at night

hood_desc: The walkable heart around Plaza Independencia and the pedestrianised Sarmiento avenue, lined with cafés, wine bars and plane-tree-shaded plazas; the easiest base for first-time visitors.

The city's historic birthplace around Pedro del Castillo square, home to the Área Fundacional Museum and the ruins of colonial Mendoza; quiet, atmospheric and steeped in the city's earthquake history.
A leafy, upscale residential district beside the huge Parque General San Martín, good for joggers, families and travellers who want green space and calm a short walk from downtown.
A bohemian wine village in Luján de Cuyo just south of the city, known for its Sunday antiques fair, leafy plaza, boutique bodegas and a lively weekend bar-and-restaurant scene.
A busy adjoining suburb with the Palmares shopping-and-dining strip and easy Metrotranvía access; a good-value, local-feeling base with plenty of restaurants and nightlife.

water.note: Andes-fed tap water is safe to drink, though many visitors prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30 AM to midnight; the Metrotranvía light rail runs about 6 AM to 11 PM with reduced weekend service.
transit.pay: Fares are paid with the rechargeable RedBus/SUBE contactless card (most buses no longer take cash); tap on boarding. Cards are sold at kiosks and terminals.
transit.note: Greater Mendoza is served by the MendoTran bus network and a single north–south Metrotranvía light-rail line linking Las Heras, the city centre, Godoy Cruz and Maipú.

air: Governor Francisco Gabrielli International Airport (MDZ / El Plumerillo)
bus: Mendoza bus terminal (Terminal del Sol) for intercity & international coaches

airport.name: Governor Francisco Gabrielli International Airport (MDZ / El Plumerillo)

transit.m: Local bus (line 680) to the city centre (~30-40 min)
Taxi/remis to the city centre (15-20 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants (the 'cubierto' cover charge is separate); rounding up taxi fares is common.
